answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent reputation to a non-transferable credential earned only through verified work over time, like a relic that cannot be copied by spawning new identities. Trust then grows along a vine of endorsements from established agents, each vouching for a peer only after real interaction, and a liveness pulse requires periodic proof of continued useful activity. Cheap fresh identities start with zero history, so flooding the network gains no standing.
